intent.instructions: Classify the search in `query` — a user question, an agent task, or a code-analysis goal — into exactly one intent. `criteria` names the intent and the tool that answers it. Choose the narrowest intent that still answers the request; when a behavior is described but no identifier is known, choose `unknown_implementation` instead of inventing a literal.

criteria.literal: An exact string the caller already knows — a message, error text, identifier fragment, or config value. rg matches the bytes; no AST.
criteria.symbol: A function, method, class, variable, or module name the caller knows. rg finds every occurrence; when the query is also a code shape, ast-grep adds the declaration/usage structure.
criteria.call: Call or invocation sites of a known function or method (who calls X). ast-grep matches call expressions; rg alone confuses declarations, imports, and strings.
criteria.type: A class, struct, interface, enum, or type declaration. ast-grep matches the declaration structure.
criteria.config: A configuration key, value, environment variable, setting, or flag. rg matches the text in config and source files; no AST.
criteria.todo: TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK notes or other comment text. rg matches the comment bytes; no AST.
criteria.pattern: A structural code shape rather than a name — a call with an argument, a control-flow form, a nested literal. ast-grep matches the syntax tree.
criteria.unknown_implementation: A behavior or capability with no known identifier ("where is retry handled"). rg locates candidate files and lines first; ast-grep refines them when the query also carries a code shape.
criteria.cross_language: The same concept across several languages (an HTTP client in Python and Go). rg finds candidates everywhere first; ast-grep refines per language when a code shape is available.
